title: Comparative outcomes require common denominators
summary: A comparison and inference protocol: 24 entities now carry vertical evidence layers, one-record coverage decisions, repeated acquisition results, and bounded partial-closure deepening while identity, compatibility, attribution, validation status, denominator breaks, and continuation rules remain attached.
map_question: When can operating records support a comparison, and when must they remain parallel evidence trails?
interpretation_boundary: The map governs within-domain longitudinal claims. It is not a score, ranking, forecast, or claim that different operating systems share one outcome direction.

nodes.label: AI and cyber outcomes
nodes.note: Inventory, maturity, implementation, incident, and benefit measures remain distinct.

nodes.label: Manufacturing outcomes
nodes.note: Participation, completion, placement, sales, savings, jobs, quality, and productivity use different denominators.

nodes.label: Infrastructure outcomes
nodes.note: Capacity, service, reliability, commodity, and water measures answer different questions.

nodes.label: Mobility and mission outcomes
nodes.note: Trips, flights, miles, incidents, operations, missions, and cargo must retain system context.

nodes.label: Unit and denominator
nodes.note: The quantity and population or exposure base must match.

nodes.label: Period, geography, and method
nodes.note: Records must cover compatible time, place, scope, and collection rules.

nodes.label: Attribution and validation
nodes.note: Official, audited, company-attributed, and modeled results must remain labeled.

nodes.label: Comparable outcome evidence
nodes.note: Comparison begins only after the measurement contracts align.

nodes.label: Compatible time points
nodes.note: At least two observations must share the measurement contract before direction is described.

nodes.label: Revisions and series breaks
nodes.note: Vintages, method changes, combined years, and discontinued definitions remain first-class evidence.

nodes.label: Bounded longitudinal read
nodes.note: Direction is published inside one defined series without becoming a composite score.

nodes.label: Stable entity identity
nodes.note: Agency, facility, plant code, or operating-carrier identity must persist across observations.

nodes.label: Bounded entity operating panel
nodes.note: At least two compatible observations can publish inside one named entity without becoming a rank.

nodes.label: Entity driver and constraint dossier
nodes.note: Baseline, intervention or input, constraint, and later observation are ordered inside one stable entity.

nodes.label: Causal-inference hold
nodes.note: Attribution and temporal sequence do not establish an independently validated causal effect.

nodes.label: Repeat outcome or alternative-explanation test
nodes.note: A later record maps to named alternatives and declares compatibility, attribution, and validation status.

nodes.label: Denominator or method break
nodes.note: Different units, methods, identities, windows, and attribution levels stop silent series extension.

nodes.label: Four-record entity sufficiency screen
nodes.note: A candidate enters only when stable identity and at least four primary or official records support all three layers.

nodes.label: Second-cohort panel, dossier, and test
nodes.note: All twelve retained entities carry the same three-layer publication contract.

nodes.label: 24-entity one-record coverage ledger
nodes.note: One record is Closed, sixteen are Partially Closed, and seven remain Open under named reopening rules.

nodes.label: Seven exact-record acquisition checks
nodes.note: Dalrymple advances to Partially Closed; six selected records remain Open under dated continuation rules.

nodes.label: Fourteen acquisition and deepening decisions
nodes.note: DOE, F-35, and Hornsdale advance to Partially Closed; three exact rails remain Open and eight partial records deepen.

A material series break stops or restates the line.

Entity panels remain bounded and do not close cross-entity comparability.

Alternative explanations and validation limits remain attached to every association.
Repeated compatible outcomes and independent validation are incomplete.

Twelve of twelve candidates passed the four-record screen.
The vertical contract preserves method, attribution, identity, and denominator breaks.
Four portfolio interpretations remain held even though all 36 entity layers publish.
A coverage decision cannot bridge an incompatible unit, denominator, period, method, identity, or attribution break.

Six checked sources remain incompatible with the selected annual, monthly, interval, investigation, or restoration record.

what_this_map_supports: FTFN can publish bounded outcome records while preserving their original measurement contracts.
Within-domain comparisons may proceed when unit, denominator, period, geography, method, and attribution align.
Explicit holds identify where activity or reporting structure has not become a comparable outcome.
A direction statement may publish after at least two compatible observations, with a two-point caveat.
Revisions and method breaks can stop, split, or restate a longitudinal series.
A named entity panel may publish after stable identity and at least two compatible observations are verified.
National context and entity performance remain separate layers.
A stable entity panel may deepen into a temporally ordered driver and constraint dossier.
Attribution, independent validation, and alternative explanations can be published without claiming causation.
A later record may narrow, support, challenge, or leave unresolved a named alternative explanation.
Regulator-verified obligations, partial progress, company claims, operator filings, and independent outcomes can remain distinct.
A second cohort can be screened once and then built vertically through the same three evidence layers.
Independent, regulator, operator, company, and carrier-attributed records can remain visibly distinct inside one entity dossier.
A one-record-per-entity acquisition queue with explicit closure states and reopening rules.
A dated acquisition trail showing which named reopening conditions did and did not change evidence state.
A dated trail showing three bounded Open-to-Partially-Closed advances and eight partial-record deepenings.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not create a cross-portfolio score or ranking.
It does not equate activity, capacity, exposure, service, reliability, safety, cost, or local benefit.
It does not convert company-attributed results into audited causal effects.
It does not turn a two-point movement into a durable trend.
It does not authorize normalization across incompatible domains.
It does not authorize a cross-agency, cross-manufacturer, cross-asset, or cross-carrier ranking.
It does not prove that a named intervention, control, input, commitment, or corrective action caused an observed outcome.
It does not authorize a readiness score, composite score, or entity ranking.
It does not prove that one tested alternative caused the observed outcome.
It does not authorize denominator mixing, causal effects, rankings, composites, or readiness scores.
It does not make the two cohorts or their entities rankable.
It does not convert vertical evidence depth into a causal effect, composite, or readiness score.
That a Closed, Partially Closed, or Open coverage state measures entity performance, readiness, safety, quality, value, or relative standing.
That a current index, governance audit, cumulative total, capacity record, queue entry, or historical extract closes a different operating question.
That a management letter, annual total, cumulative fleet count, recommendation state, ongoing investigation, or constraint event is a complete operating or outcome record.
